status: DRAFT answer key: written with the corpus, to be reviewed and signed off by the author before scoring.

must_find.why: The practice (custodian) is established in Valdora, a Member State (Annex I).
Art 8(2)(c) health-care condition on the basis of Member State law: VHIA 4(1) registered practitioners; VHIA 4(2) the agent acting on documented instructions is under their responsibility.
6(1)(b) contract: patients pay under terms of care. 6(1)(f) legitimate interests is unavailable for sensitive information (6(2)).
Signed agreement covers the 9(2) terms; its deletion term interacts with CHRA 9 (see conflicts).

routes.APIR 17 recognition: ruled_out: Annex II recognition of Corvel extends only to non-sensitive information, despite the active certificate
routes.APIR 18 approved clauses: unmet as described: clauses executed, but no 18(2) assessment, and Corvel law (CRAA 3, 4, 6) allows secret production orders without court authorisation; with Northgate holding the keys no effective supplementary measure exists, so 18(3) bars the transfer
routes.APIR 19 derogations: ruled_out: the transfer is ongoing, so 19(1)(a)-(b) are excluded by 19(2); (c) and (d) do not fit

must_find.cure: Keep the decryption keys only within the Union (CRAA 5 then removes the compelled-decryption risk), document the 18(2) assessment, and stop Northgate engineers in Corvel opening plaintext records (support without key access, or practice-mediated).

must_find.why: Cumulative Valdora condition (Art 8(3)): 30 days' prior notification to the Commission (not done) and Union-held keys (keys are held by Northgate in Corvel).
3,200 patients is below the 5,000 threshold in APIR 12(2)(a), but VHIA 8(a) requires an assessment for hosting a patient record system outside Valdora regardless of numbers; none was prepared.
Notice names the third territory and the route relied on.
Northgate is a data host; it must keep records 7 years unless it returns records that originated outside Corvel and keeps no copy (9(2)). The agreement says delete within 30 days.
The practice bills no Corvel insurer, so it is not a covered provider and Northgate is not its service agent (CHRA 3(2)); CHRA 4-8 do not apply.

conflicts.resolution: The custodian chooses return rather than deletion under APIR 9(2)(f); returning records that originated outside Corvel and keeping no copy satisfies CHRA 9(2).

cross_jurisdiction.about: Public-authority access in Corvel for the APIR 18(2) assessment

must_not: Treat the Corvel Trusted Recipient Scheme certificate as a valid Article 17 route for health records.
Require an impact assessment only because of APIR 12(2)(a) numbers (3,200 < 5,000), or skip it because of them.
Rely on Article 19(1)(a) consent or 19(1)(b) contract for an ongoing hosting arrangement.
Rely on Article 6(1)(f) legitimate interests for health records.
Apply CHRA 4-8 to the practice or to Northgate.
Treat a child-consent age rule (APIR 7(2), VHIA 9) as engaged: no ground relies on consent.
